gaps: No morphology evidence was assessed in this batch.
Reproduction, development, lifespan and other life-history traits have not been assessed.

claims.text: At Mt. Bontoc, five tarsiers were opportunistically observed in August 2021 and six were recorded during January–February 2022 (two direct sightings and four camera-trap records); the authors could not confirm that the records represented distinct individuals, and they stated that population viability was unknown.
claims.locator: Results, Tarsier sightings; Discussion, Tarsiers in Mt. Bontoc, Hindang
claims.placeTimeScope: Mt. Bontoc forest fragment, Hindang, Leyte, Philippines; opportunistic records in August 2021 and targeted camera trapping/field visits in January–February 2022 after Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021.
claims.lifeStatus: Free-ranging tarsiers recorded by direct observation and camera traps; the number of unique individuals was not confirmed. No captive or domesticated individuals were included.

claims.text: At five plots around confirmed tarsier sightings in Mt. Bontoc, researchers measured 612 stems; the samples had mean diameter at breast height of 2.5 cm and mean height of 5.0 m. The authors described the site as regenerating secondary forest over limestone.
claims.locator: Materials and methods, Tarsier Documentation and Habitat Survey; Results, Habitat Characteristics and Table 1
claims.placeTimeScope: Five 5-m-radius plots around sighting trees/saplings in Mt. Bontoc, Hindang, Leyte; vegetation was surveyed in the study period reported for 2021–2022.
claims.lifeStatus: Habitat measurements were made at locations where free-ranging tarsiers were confirmed; measurements do not represent all habitats used by the species.

gaps: This is a localized survey from one forest fragment; it does not establish species-wide habitat use or a complete geographic range.
The study did not estimate population size or viability, and the observed records may not represent distinct individuals.
Reproduction, morphology, evolution, fossil evidence and independent conservation assessments were not assessed in this batch.
No phylogenetic or evolutionary evidence was assessed.
A species-wide distribution inventory was not assessed; observations at Mt. Bontoc do not define the species range.
No fossil evidence or geological age was assessed.
No threat status, trend or range-wide conservation assessment was assessed.

reasons: One localized field study provides bounded ecological observations; other facets remain not-assessed.
The observations do not establish unique population counts, population viability or a species-wide account.
No independent expert review has been completed.
